entries.title: Genesis 16:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Sarai, being barren, gives Hagar to Abram. 4 Hagar, being afflicted for despising her mistress, runs away. 7 An angel commands her to return and submit herself, promises her a numerous posterity, and shows their character and condition. 13 Hagar names the place, and returns to Sarai. 15 Ishmael is born. 16 The age of Abram.

A.M. 2092. B.C. 1912. bare. 15:2,3; 21:10,12; 25:21; Jud 13:2; Lu 1:7,36 Egyptian. 12:16; 21:9,21 name. Ga 4:24 Agar.

entries.title: Genesis 16:7
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: found. Pr 15:3 the fountain. 25:18; Ex 15:22; 1Sa 15:7 Shur.The desert of Shur being between the south of Canaan, where Hebron was situated, and Egypt, it is likely that Hagar was returning to her own country.

entries.content: Sarai's maid. 1,4; Eph 6:5-8; 1Ti 6:1,2 whence. 3:9; 4:10; Ec 10:4; Jer 2:17,18 I flee. 1Sa 26:19

entries.title: Genesis 16:12
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
be a. 21:20; Job 11:12; 39:5-8 wild.The word rendered "wild" also denotes the "wild ass;" the description of which animal in Job 39:5-8, affords the very best representation of the wandering, lawless, freebooting life of the Bedouin and other Arabs, the descendants of Ishmael.
